sources.locator: "Battle of Sandepu", revision 1370588463, § Background and § The Battle of Sandepu

explanation: Sandepu's § Background gives the reason for the offensive: Kuropatkin "was concerned about the impending arrival of the battle-hardened Japanese Third Army under General Nogi Maresuke to the front after the fall of Port Arthur on 2 January 1905", and § The Battle of Sandepu gives its timing from the same fact: "On 19 January, Kuropatkin issued orders for the Second Manchurian Army to attack in a maneuver to outflank General Oku's Japanese Second Army and to drive it back across the Taitzu River before Nogi's Third Army could arrive." The siege ends on 2 January and the attack opens on 25 January, so the reaction is datable as well as stated. Probable: Wikipedia alone.
